spice up the lesson: Our English teacher likes to spice up the lesson with funny videos and games, so nobody falls asleep.
我們的英文老師喜歡用有趣的影片和遊戲讓課程更有趣，所以沒有人會打瞌睡。
spice up one's life: After retiring, my father decided to spice up his life by learning salsa dancing and traveling abroad.
退休後，我爸爸決定學騷莎舞並出國旅行，為生活增添情趣。
spice the dish: My mother likes to spice the dish with garlic, pepper, and a little chili to make it smell wonderful.
我媽媽喜歡用大蒜、胡椒和一點辣椒為菜餚加香料，讓它聞起來香極了。
variety is the spice of life: I take a different route to school every week, because variety is the spice of life.
我每週都走不同的路線上學，因為變化是生活的調味料。
spill the beans: We planned a surprise party for Mom, but my little brother spilled the beans at dinner.
我們為媽媽籌劃了一場驚喜派對，但我弟弟在晚餐時洩密了。
spill over into violence: The police worried that the angry argument between the two groups might spill over into violence.
警方擔心兩群人之間激烈的爭吵可能演變成暴力。
spill blood: The two leaders signed a peace agreement because neither side wanted to spill blood any longer.
兩位領袖簽署了和平協議，因為雙方都不想再流血了。
the crowd spilled into the street: When the concert hall became too full, the crowd spilled into the street to watch on big screens.
音樂廳擠滿了人之後，人群湧上街頭，透過大螢幕觀看。
spill one's guts: After hours of questions, the nervous boy finally spilled his guts and told the teacher everything.
經過好幾個小時的詢問，緊張的男孩終於全盤托出，把一切都告訴了老師。
cry over spilt milk: You failed the quiz, but there is no use crying over spilt milk; just study harder next time.
你小考不及格了，但為打翻的牛奶哭泣沒有用，下次更用功就好。
spin a story: When students come to class late, some of them like to spin a story about helping an old lady.
學生上課遲到時，有些人喜歡編故事，說自己在幫助一位老太太。
spin out of control: The car hit a patch of ice and began to spin out of control on the mountain road.
車子壓到一片冰，開始在山路上打轉失控。
spin the news: Some politicians try to spin the news so that their mistakes look like great successes.
有些政客試圖操弄新聞角度，讓他們的錯誤看起來像是巨大的成功。
spin a web: In the early morning, we watched a spider spin a web between two branches in the garden.
清晨時，我們看著一隻蜘蛛在花園的兩根樹枝之間結網。
spin off a company: The big tech firm decided to spin off a company that would focus only on electric cars.
那家大型科技公司決定分拆出一家只專注於電動車的公司。
spin a coin: We couldn't agree on who should go first, so we decided to spin a coin on the table.
我們無法決定誰應該先開始，所以決定在桌上轉硬幣。
my head is spinning: After three hours of math problems, my head is spinning and I really need a short break.
做了三個小時的數學題後，我頭昏腦脹，真的需要休息一下。
split the bill: When we eat out together, my friends and I usually split the bill so that everyone pays the same.
我和朋友一起外出用餐時，通常會分攤帳單，讓每個人付一樣的錢。
split up: After dating for three years, the couple decided to split up because they wanted different things in life.
交往三年後，這對情侶決定分手，因為他們在人生中想要的東西不同。
split hairs: Let's not split hairs about whether the meeting starts at 2:00 or 2:05; just be there on time.
我們別吹毛求疵爭論會議是兩點還是兩點零五分開始了，準時到就好。
split the difference: He wanted to sell the bike for 3,000 dollars and I offered 2,000, so we split the difference at 2,500.
他想以三千元賣腳踏車，我出價兩千，所以我們各讓一半，以兩千五成交。
split one's sides: The comedian's jokes were so funny that the whole audience nearly split their sides laughing.
那位喜劇演員的笑話太好笑了，全場觀眾幾乎笑破肚皮。
split the vote: Having two similar candidates in the election may split the vote and help the third candidate win.
選舉中有兩位相似的候選人可能會分散選票，讓第三位候選人獲勝。
a split second: For a split second, I thought I saw my old friend in the crowd, but then he disappeared.
有一瞬間，我以為我在人群中看到了老朋友，但接著他就不見了。
split into groups: The teacher asked us to split into groups of four and discuss the story we had just read.
老師要我們分組，四人一組，討論我們剛剛讀的故事。
spoil a child: Giving a kid everything he asks for will spoil a child and make him unable to accept failure.
孩子要什麼就給什麼會寵壞小孩，讓他無法接受失敗。
spoil the fun: Please don't tell everyone how the movie ends, or you will spoil the fun for the rest of us.
請不要告訴大家電影的結局，不然你會讓我們其他人掃興。
spoil the surprise: Don't post the birthday photos online yet, or you will spoil the surprise before Amy gets home.
先別把生日照片發到網路上，否則在艾咪回家前你就會破壞驚喜。
food spoils: In hot summer weather, food spoils quickly if you leave it on the kitchen table for hours.
在炎熱的夏天，如果你把食物放在廚房餐桌上好幾個小時，食物很快就會壞掉。
spoil one's appetite: Don't eat so many cookies before dinner, or you will spoil your appetite for the meal.
晚餐前別吃那麼多餅乾，否則你會影響食慾，吃不下正餐。
be spoiled for choice: With over fifty food stalls at the night market, visitors will be spoiled for choice every evening.
夜市有五十多個小吃攤，遊客每晚都會選擇多到眼花。
spoil the view: Many people worry that the ugly new tower will spoil the view of the mountains from the lake.
許多人擔心那座醜陋的新大樓會破壞從湖邊眺望山景的景觀。
